pr_title: Ajax: remove extra "?" in the URL

issue_context.title: $.getJSON treats request as JSONP when URL contains ?? (two question marks)
issue_context.body:
Originally reported by Stijn at: http://bugs.jquery.com/ticket/15216

Similar to http://bugs.jquery.com/ticket/8417 and its duplicates, but they're all about the data parameter, not the URL parameter.

Happens with current stable and with edge. Fiddle:  http://jsfiddle.net/r5zcw6wx/

Code: 

$.getJSON("http://date.jsontest.com/")
$.getJSON("http://date.jsontest.com/?foo")
$.getJSON("http://date.jsontest.com/??foo")

Requests: 

GET http://date.jsontest.com/
GET http://date.jsontest.com/?foo
GET http://date.jsontest.com/jQuery2129957077760988448071399739372034175163514043816_1408610547781foo?_=1408610547782

Of course we shouldn't be making requests with two question marks (naive string concat on our side), and this could be a dupe of the mentioned ticket, but I figured this was worth reporting anyway.

Issue reported for jQuery 2.1.1

review_comments:
Perhaps `/\?\?+/` would be faster as in this PR you're currently changing single question marks to themselves.
Yeah right, but it's not a problem if this url change?
`"/file.html?q=??"`
Ah, I see, you're changing the first question mark only and that's why it needs to be one. Seems fine as it is then.
Actually it isn't. The `??` replacer was introduced so that you can handle APIs with callbacks as part of the url: `http://api.site.ext/path/to/method/callback=??`.

We had problems with those back in the days.

Not sure what we're trying to fix here... `http://somesite.ext/path/to/page??something=something` is not valid and jQuery is not in the business of handling invalid entries.
@jaubourg: i never do some `jsonp` but it's not only these cases:
`index.html?callback=?`
`index.html?var=1&callback=?`
`http://ex.com/?callback=?` and dont find where we have to write two `?`.
http://bugs.jquery.com/ticket/4897
@jaubourg oh.. ok.
I read these tests: https://github.com/jquery/jquery/blob/master/test/unit/ajax.js#L704
Finally, I don't understand exactly what is it necessary for doing some `jsonp`...
The doc http://api.jquery.com/jquery.ajax/ doesn't speak about `??` anywhere :(
Not the first time we forgot to document something ;)

Not sure I understand your question but the fix (ie introduction of `??`) was for APIs that would have the callback as part of the URL, not as a parameter (see [the original ticket](http://bugs.jquery.com/ticket/4897)).
Ahhhh I understood :)

It's really different with that behaviour :/
Because if we want to be friendly on `.html??var=` we have to be also friendly on `/callback=???var=` and `/callback=?/??var=` the regex is more complex and maybe it's not so necessary.

I think we have to use this regex: `.replace( /([^=]|=\?)\?+/, "$1?" )`
(some tests here: http://jsfiddle.net/Mr21/0sofoaay/)
Well, to be honest, I think we shouldn't try and fix anything because it is working as intended. The original bug report is bogus in that it is asking to cater to an illformed url.
